LESSON: HUMAN ORIGIN

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People, Population and Relationships
Topic 2.1: Human Origin
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human Origin, part of People, Population and Relationships in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How did human beings come to be?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explore traditional stories of human origin from African communities,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Origin in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the religious stories about the origin of humankind,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Origin in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. formulate common aspects from traditional and religious stories of human origin for self- identity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Origin in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the various stories of human origin for self-identity. ● Learners are guided to engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human origin from their communities. ● In groups, learners are guided to compare the different stories on human origin from their communities and share in class. ● Learners are guided to write a collaborative essay on traditional and religious stories of human origin. ● In groups or with a peer, learners are guided to use How did human beings come to be? 9 print, braille or electronic media resources to research and present in class the religious stories about the origin of humankind. ● In groups or with a peer, learners are guided to record traditional stories about the origin of humankind in society, ● In groups, learners are guided to discuss ways of recording traditional stories about the origin of humankind in society.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Origin in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Human Origin helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

   Human Origin helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. formulate common aspects from traditional and religious stories of human origin for self- identity,

   Human Origin helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge the various stories of human origin for self-identity. ● Learners are guided to engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human origin from their communities. ● In groups, learners are guided to compare the different stories on human origin from their communities and share in class. ● Learners are guided to write a collaborative essay on traditional and religious stories of human origin. ● In groups or with a peer, learners are guided to use How did human beings come to be? 9 print, braille or electronic media resources to research and present in class the religious stories about the origin of humankind. ● In groups or with a peer, learners are guided to record traditional stories about the origin of humankind in society, ● In groups, learners are guided to discuss ways of recording traditional stories about the origin of humankind in society.

   Human Origin helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human Origin together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: Learners develop writing and teamwork skills as they write collaborative essays on

human origin from their communities and share in class.

● Citizenship: Learners acquire cultural identity skills as they engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and

religious stories on human origin from their communities

10

Values:
● Responsibility: Learners engage in assigned roles and duties as they work in groups to compare different stories on

human origin.

● Patriotism: Learners obey laws and regulation as they write a collaborative essay on traditional and religious stories of

human origin.

● Respect: Learners appreciate diverse opinions as they engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious

stories on human origin.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self-Esteem: Learners use relevant print or braille and electronic media resources to research and present in class

the religious stories about the origin of humankind.

● Social Cohesion: Learners work in groups to compare different stories on human origin.

Link to other subjects:

● English, Kiswahili, Kenyan Sign Language: Learners write a collaborative essay on traditional and religious stories

of human origin

● Religious Education: Learners engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human

origin.

11

Suggested Learning resources:

● Resource persons, maps, digital resources with assistive technology, tactile maps, embossed charts, spur wheel, approved

textbooks and other printed or braille resources.

Main points to remember:

3. formulate common aspects from traditional and religious stories of human origin for self- identity,
